sections.overview: The Black Redstart is a widespread Eurasian songbird that has adapted from rocky landscapes to towns and buildings.
sections.identification: The spring male is mostly dark, with a pale wing patch and a rusty-red tail; the species is about 14 cm long.
sections.habitat: It originally occupied rocky and mountainous terrain but is now common in built-up areas as well.
sections.diet: It catches insects and larvae, often in quick sallies, and may eat berries in autumn.
sections.behavior: In Britain it occurs year-round, but records peak during autumn passage; a few birds overwinter.
sections.reproduction: It nests in cavities or on building structures and can raise two or three broods in a year.
sections.ecology: It belongs to the same genus as the Common Redstart (Phoenicurus phoenicurus); the male Black Redstart is dark, while the other species has an orange breast.
sections.conservation: The consulted accounts describe a broad distribution; they do not establish a current global population trend here.
